rows.description: A child receiving a reprimand may look down, argue, cry or go silent, and the reaction does not prove guilt or indifference. Adults do better focusing on the behaviour and the fix rather than shame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, shame, guilt

rows.description: A school-age child faced with an accusation or gossip can pause, ask for facts and check with the adult or person involved. Quick belief in a claim, or hitting back, tends to escalate hurt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child recognises repeated taunting, threats or exclusion as bullying, avoids retaliating, stays near safe people and tells a trusted adult. Being targeted is never the child's fault.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Playful teasing among friends can shift into mocking or ridicule when one person is hurt or cannot laugh along. Watching the target's face, the power balance and repetition helps children tell fun from unkind, and they should tell an adult about ongoing harm.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, playfulness, hurt

rows.description: A child proposes turns, splitting time or trading choices, such as "You pick this game, I pick the next". Compromise works when both sides feel heard and the deal is remembered.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child argues "Everyone else is allowed" or "I finished my homework, so..." to persuade. Reasons can be valid or exaggerated, and adults can respond to the argument while noting the limits.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child learns to notice appeals like "everyone does it" or pressure to decide quickly. Asking "What is the reason?" and taking time is a sound habit, and a pushed dare or secret should be told to a trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child shares secrets and feelings with a close friend, building trust. Children need to learn which secrets are safe to keep and that any secret about harm or fear should be told to a trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child explains "I did it because..." to justify actions, mixing real reasons and excuses. Listening for the need behind the explanation helps, without treating every reason as proof of intent.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child says "I ate a million pizzas" or tells a tall tale for effect. Exaggeration shows play with truth and the child's ability to know it is not real; it is different from lying when both sides share the joke.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
